name: Wavelet Packet Decomposition
description: Applies full wavelet packet decomposition for fine-grained sub-band energy analysis (Coifman & Wickerhauser, 1992).
mechanism:
This method applies Wavelet Packet Decomposition (WPD) following Coifman & Wickerhauser (1992) for comprehensive frequency-domain forensic analysis:

1. **Full Wavelet Packet Tree**: Unlike standard DWT (which only decomposes the approximation subband), WPD recursively decomposes both approximation and detail subbands, creating a full binary tree of 2ⁿ subbands at depth n. This provides uniform frequency resolution across the entire spectrum.

2. **Best Basis Selection**: The optimal basis is selected via entropy-based cost function (Shannon entropy, log-energy, or threshold counting) minimization over the packet tree. The best basis structure itself is forensically informative — natural images optimize differently than AI-generated ones.

3. **Subband Energy Distribution**: Energy distribution across all wavelet packet subbands is computed. Natural images follow predictable energy decay patterns related to the 1/f spectral falloff. AI artifacts produce anomalous energy in specific subbands — GAN grid artifacts appear as energy peaks at characteristic spatial frequencies.

4. **Inter-Subband Correlation Analysis**: Cross-correlations between sibling and parent-child subbands capture statistical dependencies inherent in natural images. AI-generated images often exhibit altered inter-subband correlation structures — either excessive independence (failing to replicate natural dependencies) or artificial correlations from generator architectures.

5. **Coefficient Distribution Profiling**: Wavelet packet coefficient distributions at each node are modeled. Natural image coefficients follow generalized Gaussian distributions with scale-dependent parameters. Deviations from these models — particularly in high-frequency subbands where AI generators struggle to reproduce correct statistics — are quantified for forensic scoring.

accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.

limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
